random-selection.def: Choosing individuals by a chance process, such as a random number generator, so that no one’s judgment decides who is chosen.

srs.def: A simple random sample (SRS) of size n is chosen so that every group of n individuals in the population has the same chance of being the sample.

replacement.def: Sampling without replacement means an individual can be chosen once; with replacement, an individual is returned and can be chosen again.

stratified.def: A stratified random sample splits the population into strata, groups of similar individuals, and takes a simple random sample from each stratum.

cluster-sample.def: A cluster sample splits the population into groups (clusters), chooses some clusters at random, and measures every individual in the chosen clusters.

systematic.def: A systematic random sample chooses a random starting point in an ordered list and then takes every kth individual.

sampling-frame.def: The list of individuals from which a sample is actually chosen, such as a roster, a map or a list of addresses.
